Name: Angie Muse
Badge: Reading to Write: Say-Mean-Matter
How might you introduce Say-Mean-Matter to your students? What about this framework do you think will be helpful for them? What might be challenging?:

I will use the Say-Mean-Matter strategy in PD with Rockwood teachers in January. We will have teachers read text sets and we need a variety of text response strategies. This is a perfect strategy to use with an argument. The Matter portion of the thinking can help students evaluate evidence for their argument. In other words, when they note a sleep expert saying that we don't all need 8 hours of sleep, they need to ask themselves not only what this opinion means but also what does this expert opinion matter in the conversation about sleep. This strategy will help students not only catalogue evidence but also think deeply about how that evidence relates to the argument.

I am also going to use this strategy in my UMSL course on disciplinary literacy. Just like theThey Say-I Say framework, the Say-Mean-Matter framework is more than the sum of its parts. This strategy deserves some pedagogical attention from my students who are about to have classrooms of their own.
